newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chips rise in quiet market before election.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chips rise in quiet market before election.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks posted modest gains Monday as pre-election jitters quelled activity in all but a few shares.

At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 18.26 points at 6,040.19. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a small margin on light volume of 214 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index slipped 0.57 of a point at 1,221.21. The American Stock Exchange index was off 0.82 at 571.76.

Despite the announcement of the massive merger of MCI Communications Corp. and British Telecom, analysts said investors seemed intent on sitting out the final session ahead of Election Day except where circumstances dictated otherwise.

"People are saying, 'Let's get the election behind us,'" said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Van Kampen American Capital. "I think the mentality is something has to be really dramatic to move anything."

The re-election of President Clinton was generally seen as a foregone conclusion, but Wall Street was still afraid that a Democratic sweep of both the House and Senate would unleash a bearish market reaction.
Aside from the election, the spotlight was on mergers.

MCI rose 1/2 to 30-3/4 in its first trading since Friday afternoon, when the shares were halted ahead of the company's announcement Sunday that it would be acquired by British Telecommunications Plc in the biggest trans-Atlantic deal ever.
British Telecoms' American Depositary Shares surged, gaining 5-3/4 to 61-1/4 on the NYSE.

United Carolina Bancshares jumped 9-1/4 to 36-3/4 after that company agreed to be acquired by Southern National Corp. in a stock swap valued at $985 million, or about $40 per share. Southern National fell 1-1/2 to 33-3/4.
Sierra Health Services Inc. skidded 4-1/4 to 24-5/8 after the company agreed to buy Physician Corp. of America. Physician, which also announced a third-quarter loss, rose 1/8 to 10-3/4.

Conrail Inc. fell 3 to 92-1/4 on news that its rival suitors CSX Corp. and Norfolk Southern Corp. were holding talks over their competing bids for Conrail, dampening hopes among Conrail shareholders that a protracted bidding war would emerge for the railroad.
CSX shares climbed 1-5/8 to 44-5/8 and Norfolk Southern gained 1-1/4 to 90-5/8.
J.C. Penney Co. dipped 2-3/4 to 50-1/4 one day after announcing it would acquire Eckerd Corp. for cash and stock in a two-step deal valued at $3.3 billion. Eckerd soared 4 to 32-7/8.
